# 1.1 Overview

## Key Requirements and Definitions

- **NVMe Interface**: Enables communication between a host and a non-volatile memory subsystem (NVM subsystem).
- **Supported Transports**: Optimized for various transports including **PCI Express®, Ethernet, InfiniBand™, and Fibre Channel**.
- **Transport Binding**: Mapping of NVMe extensions to specific transports is defined in **NVMe Transport binding specifications**. For Fibre Channel, this is specified in **INCITS 556 FC-NVMe-2**.
- **Revision Changes**: Changes from **Revision 2.2 to 2.3** and new mandatory requirements are documented at: [https://nvmexpress.org/specification/nvm-express-revision-changes](https://nvmexpress.org/specification/nvm-express-revision-changes).

## NVM Express® Specification Family (1.1.1)

The NVMe specification family includes:

1. **NVM Express Base Specification** (this document):  
   - Defines a protocol for host-to-NVM subsystem communication over **memory-based and message-based transports**.

2. **NVM Express Management Interface (NVMe-MI)**:  
   - Optional management interface for all NVMe subsystems.

3. **NVM Express I/O Command Set Specifications**:  
   - Extend the Base Specification with data structures, features, log pages, commands, and status values.

4. **NVM Express Transport Specifications**:  
   - Define binding of NVMe protocol (including controller properties) to specific transports.

5. **NVM Express Boot Specification**:  
   - Provides constructs and guidelines for booting from NVMe interfaces.

> **Note**: The family structure (Figure 1) illustrates **applicability**, not hierarchy, protocol stack, or system architecture.

title: Scope
summary:
# 1.2 Scope

> **Section ID**: 1.2 | **Page**: 26-26

This specification defines the interface requirements for communication with a controller in an NVM subsystem, including properties and commands that must be implemented by a controller using a specific NVMe Transport. It also specifies common aspects of the NVMe I/O Command Sets that may be supported.

Three types of controllers are defined, each with distinct capabilities (refer to Section 3.1.3):

- **I/O controllers**  
- **Discovery controllers**  
- **Administrative controllers**

The term "controller" is used generically throughout the document unless context requires a specific type.

> **Section ID**: 1.3 | **Page**: 26-26

## Key Points

- **Usage Models**: Not specified or licensed. Examples include SSD, main memory, cache, backup, or redundant memory.
- **Implementation Details**: Implementation of requirements and behaviors (e.g., SSD with direct fabric attachment, PCIe NVMe translator, software on general-purpose server) is outside scope.

This specification defines only the communication interface to the NVM subsystem, independent of usage model, implementation, media management, or caching. All numerical values and table data are absent as no tables or quantitative data are present in this section.

# 1.4 Conventions Summary

## Keywords

- **mandatory**: Items that must be implemented as defined.
- **may**: Indicates flexibility in choice with no preference.
- **obsolete**: Functionality removed from current spec; was in previous versions.
- **optional**: Not required, but if implemented, must conform to specification.
- **R**: Abbreviation for "reserved" in figures/tables when space is limited.
- **reserved**: Bits/fields set aside for future use; must be cleared to `0h` unless specified otherwise. Receipt of reserved values in defined fields is an error. Writing reserved values to controller properties yields undefined results.
- **shall**: Mandatory requirement; must be implemented for interoperability.
- **should**: Strongly recommended; indicates flexibility with preferred alternative.

## Numerical Descriptions

- **Base**: Values are 1-based unless specified otherwise (e.g., 1h = 1, not 0h).
- **Size Units**:
  - Decimal: use **kilo (k)**, **mega (M)**, **giga (G)**, etc. (powers of 10).
  - Binary: use **kibi (Ki)**, **mebi (Mi)**, **gibi (Gi)**, etc. (powers of 2).
  - Symbols and powers:
    | Symbol      | Power (base-10) | Symbol     | Power (base-2) |
    |-------------|------------------|------------|----------------|
    | kilo / k    | 10³              | kibi / Ki  | 2¹⁰            |
    | mega / M    | 10⁶              | mebi / Mi  | 2²⁰            |
    | giga / G    | 10⁹              | gibi / Gi  | 2³⁰            |
    | tera / T    | 10¹²             | tebi / Ti  | 2⁴⁰            |
    | peta / P    | 10¹⁵             | pebi / Pi  | 2⁵⁰            |

- **Number Formats**:

  - Binary: use `b` suffix (e.g., `1001b`, `1000_0101_0010b` for >4 digits).

title: Definitions
summary:
```markdown
# 1.5 Definitions Summary

## Key Definitions and Requirements

### Admin Labels
- **admin_label**: ASCII or UTF-8 string for identifying NVMe entities (Hosts, NVM subsystems, namespaces). May include physical location, DNS name, etc.
- **admin_label_ASCII**: ASCII string (see section 1.4.2 for requirements).
- **admin_label_UTF-8**: UTF-8 string (see section 1.4.2 for requirements).

### Queues and Commands
- **Admin Queue**: Submission and Completion Queue with ID 0; used for administrative commands.
- **command_submission**: 
  - *Memory-based (e.g., PCIe)*: Completion of Submission Queue Tail Doorbell write moves tail pointer past command slot.
  - *Message-based (e.g., NVMe over Fabrics)*: Host adds capsule to Submission Queue.
- **command_completion**: Controller completes processing, updates status, and posts entry to Completion Queue.
- **I/O Command**: Submitted to I/O Submission Queue.
- **I/O Completion Queue**: Queue for I/O command completions (definition truncated).

### Controllers and Hosts
- **controller**: Interface between host and NVM subsystem. Types:
  - I/O controller
  - Discovery controller
  - Administrative controller
- **Administrative controller**: Manages NVM subsystem; no I/O queues, no namespaces, no data access.
- **Discovery controller**: Exposes Discovery Log Page; no I/O queues or data access.
- **Dynamic controller**: Allocated on-demand; no state preserved.
- **Emulated controller**: Software-defined; may or may not have physical NVMe controller.
- **Host**: Entity that submits commands to Submission Queues and retrieves completions.

### Discovery and Access
- **Centralized Discovery Controller (CDC)**: Reports discovery info registered by Direct Discovery controllers and hosts.
- **Direct Discovery Controller (DDC)**: Can register discovery info with CDC.
- **discovery_information**: Host or NVM subsystem data for discovery (e.g., NVMe Transport address, NQN).
- **Entry Key**: Fields identifying discovery info entries uniquely (refer to EKTYPE field).
- **Allowed Host List**: List of hosts (by Host NQN and Host Identifier) granted access to Exported NVM Subsystem via Exported Port.

### Exported Resources
- **Exported NVM Resources**: Includes:
  - Exported NVM Subsystems
  - Exported Namespaces
  - Exported Ports
- **Exported NVM Subsystem**: Logical subsystem exporting NVM resources; contains:
  - Zero or more Exported Namespaces
  - Zero or more controllers
  - Zero or more Exported Ports
  - May contain Allowed Host List
- **Exported Namespace**: Namespace in an Exported NVM Subsystem.
- **Exported Port**: Port exporting NVMe subsystem over fabrics transport; identified by Exported Port ID.

### Architecture & Data
- **arbitration_burst**: Max commands fetched at once by arbitration mechanism from Submission Queue.
- **arbitration_mechanism**: Determines which Submission Queue is selected next (see section 3.4.4).
- **association**: Exclusive communication between controller and host, encompassing Admin and I/O Queues.
- **cache**: Data storage area (not accessible to host) containing user data, committed or uncommitted.
- **capsule**: NVMe unit for info exchange in NVMe over Fabrics; contains command/response, data, and optional SGLs.
- **channel**: Communication path between controller and one or more Media Units.
- **directive**: Info exchange via Directive Send/Receive commands; some I/O commands may include Directive Type and Specific fields (see section 8.1.9).
- **domain**: Smallest indivisible unit sharing state (e.g., power state, capacity).
- **endurance_group**: Portion of non-volatile storage managed as a group (see section 3.2.3).
- **firmware_slot**: Location in domain storing firmware image (1–7 images per domain); shared by controllers in same domain.
- **firmware/boot partition image update command sequence**: One or more Firmware Image Download commands + Firmware Commit to commit image to slot/boot partition.

### Memory and Management
- **host-accessible_memory**: Memory accessible by host (e.g., host memory, CMB, PMR).
- **host_memory**: Read/write accessible by both host and controller; not exposed by controller (e.g., CMB, PMR); may be internal or external.
- **host_management_agent**: Host component providing external management interface (e.g., Redfish) via Admin commands (see NVM Express Management Interface Spec).
- **embedded_management_controller**: Management controller providing external interface (e.g., Redfish) via Management Endpoint commands.

### Operations and Features
- **audit**: Process to verify correct operation of sanitize (see ISO/IEC 27040, section 8.1.26).
- **authentication_commands**: Fabrics Authentication Send or Receive commands.
- **candidate_command**: Submitted command transferred to controller and ready for processing.
- **controller_reset**: Host modifies CC property to clear CC.EN from ‘1’ to ‘0’ (see section 3.7.2.1).
- **idempotent_command**: Command producing same end state and results when resubmitted (see section 9.6.3.1).
- **Configurable Device Personality (CDP)**: Host changes NVM subsystem config using personalities (see section 8.1.6).
- **dispersed_namespace**: Shared namespace accessed concurrently by controllers in ≥2 NVM subsystems (see section 8.1.10).

### Identify Data Structures
- **Identify Controller data structures**:
  - CNS 01h (Identify Controller)
  - CNS 06h (I/O Command Set specific)
- **Identify Namespace data structures**:
  - CNS 00h, CNS 09h, CNS 11h (Namespace)
  - CNS 08h, CNS 1Fh (I/O Command Set Independent)
  - CNS 05h, CNS 0Ah, CNS 1Bh (I/O Command Set specific)

### Network and Zoning
- **fabric (network fabric)**: Network topology enabling node-to-node data transfer.
- **Fabric Zoning**: Technique for configuring access control between hosts and NVM subsystems.

## Numerical Values
- **firmware_slot**: 1 to 7 images per domain.
- **Admin Queue**: Identifier 0.
- **arbitration_burst**: Max commands fetched per burst (value not specified, but defined as a limit).
```

title: Theory_of_Operation
summary:
# 2 Theory of Operation

## Key Attributes of NVMe Interface

- **Scalable Queuing**: Supports up to **65,535 I/O Queues**, each with up to **65,535 outstanding commands**.
- **Efficient Command Submission**: Requires **at most one MMIO write or one 64B message** per command submission; **no uncacheable/MMIO reads** in command path.
- **Small I/O Optimization**: All data needed to complete a **4 KiB read** is contained within the **64B command**.
- **Command Set**: Streamlined and efficient.
- **Interrupts**: Supports **MSI/MSI-X** and **interrupt aggregation**.
- **Multiple Namespaces**: Supports multiple namespaces per controller.
- **Virtualization**: Efficient support for **I/O virtualization** (e.g., SR-IOV).
- **Error Reporting**: Robust error reporting and management.
- **Multi-path I/O**: Supports **multi-path I/O and namespace sharing**.

## Controller Configuration & Properties

- **Properties** define low-level controller configuration and status (e.g., capabilities, failures, queue configuration, doorbells).
- **Transport-specific access**:
  - Memory-based transports use **registers**.
  - Message-based transports use **Property Get/Set commands**.
- **Controller capabilities** defined in:
  - **Controller Capabilities (CAP) property**
  - **Identify Controller data structure** (Figure 328)

## Transport Models

Two models for host-NVM subsystem communication:

### Memory-based Transport
- Uses explicit **memory reads/writes** (e.g., PCIe).
- Commands, responses, and data transferred via memory operations.

### Message-based Transport
- Uses **messages/capsules** (e.g., over fabric).
- Two subtypes:
  1. **Message-only**: Data transferred **only** via capsules/messages.
  2. **Message/memory**: Uses **both messages and explicit memory operations**.
- **Data may optionally be included** in command/response capsules.

> Both subtypes are collectively referred to as "message-based" when applicable.

## NVM Subsystem Architecture

- Composed of one or more **domains** (Section 3.2.5).
- May include **non-volatile storage medium** and interface to controller(s).
- **Namespaces** expose storage to hosts; each namespace has a unique identifier.
- **Controller(s)** can expose different namespaces — **not required to be identical across controllers**.
- **Discovery Service**: An NVM subsystem that supports **only Discovery controllers** (Section 3.1).

## Namespaces

- A set of resources (non-volatile storage and/or other resources) accessible via a namespace identifier.
- Each namespace has an associated **I/O Command Set**.
- **Manageability**:
  - Created/deleted via **Namespace Management** and **Capacity Management** commands.
  - **Identify Namespace** data structures define namespace-specific capabilities (Section 1.5.50).

## Command Submission & Completion

- Uses **paired Submission and Completion Queues**:
  - Host places commands in **Submission Queue**.
  - Controller places completions in **Completion Queue**.

### Command Types

| Command Type       | Purpose                                | Submit to Queue            | Notes                                                  |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| **Admin Commands** | Controller management (e.g., queue creation, abort) | Admin Submission Queue    | Only Admin or Fabrics commands allowed               |
| **I/O Commands**   | Data operations on namespaces          | I/O Submission Queue      | Uses I/O Command Set (e.g., NVM, Key Value, Zoned)   |
| **Fabrics Commands** | NVMe over Fabrics operations (e.g., connection setup, auth, property get/set) | Admin OR I/O Submission Queue | Processed **regardless of controller state (CC.EN)** |

> **Figure 5** (Types of NVMe Command Sets): Illustrates Admin, I/O, and Fabrics Command Sets. Example I/O sets: NVM, Key Value, Zoned Namespace, Computational Programs, SLM.

## Transport Taxonomy

> **Figure 4**: Shows taxonomy of transport models — **Memory-based** and **Message-based** (with subtypes: message-only and message/memory).

title: Memory-Based_Transport_Model_(PCIe)
summary:
# 2.1 Memory-Based Transport Model (PCIe)

## Key Requirements and Definitions

- **Queue Allocation**: Submission (SQ) and Completion (CQ) queues are allocated in memory.
- **Queue Creation**: Host creates queues (up to controller limit). Number of queues typically depends on system configuration (e.g., one queue pair per core in a 4-core system to avoid locking and optimize cache locality).
- **Queue Pair Mapping**: 
  - Always 1:1 mapping between Admin Submission Queue and Admin Completion Queue.
  - I/O Submission Queues can map 1:1 (Figure 6) or n:1 (Figure 7) to a single Completion Queue.
  - Multiple SQs may share one CQ for centralized processing (e.g., single worker thread handling completions).

## Architectural Details

### Submission Queue (SQ)
- **Structure**: Circular buffer with fixed slot size.
- **Command Size**: 64 bytes per command.
- **Submission**: Host submits commands by writing to SQ Tail doorbell register.
  - New doorbell write overwrites previous Tail value.
  - Controller fetches entries in order but may execute commands in any order.
- **Data Buffer Description**: 
  - Uses **PRP entries** (Physical Region Page) or **SGL (Scatter Gather List)** segments.
  - Max 2 PRP entries per command; if more needed, a pointer to a PRP List is provided.
  - Max 1 SGL segment per command; if more needed, pointer to next SGL segment is included.

### Completion Queue (CQ)
- **Structure**: Circular buffer with fixed slot size.
- **Completion Status**: Posts status for completed commands.
- **Command Identification**: Unique ID = combination of SQ ID and host-assigned command ID.
- **Processing**:
  - Host updates CQ Head pointer after processing entries.
  - **Phase Tag (P) bit** in CQ entry indicates whether entry is newly posted (without host consulting register), enabling detection of new completions.
- **Multi-SQ Support**: Multiple Submission Queues can share a single Completion Queue.

## Figures
- **Figure 6**: 1:1 SQ-to-CQ mapping (e.g., one queue pair per core).
- **Figure 7**: n:1 SQ-to-CQ mapping (multiple SQs sharing one CQ, e.g., Core B).

## Numerical Values
- Command size: **64 bytes**
- Max PRP entries per command: **2**

title: Message-Based_Transport_Model_(Fabrics)
summary:
# 2.2 Message-Based Transport Model (Fabrics)

## Key Differences from Memory-Based Model

- **1:1 Queue Mapping**: I/O Submission Queues (SQ) and I/O Completion Queues (CQ) are in one-to-one correspondence. Multiple SQs cannot map to a single CQ.
- **No Controller-Generated Interrupts**: Host fabric interface (e.g., HBA) is responsible for generating host interrupts.
- **Queue Management**: SQ and CQ creation/deletion use different mechanisms (see Section 3.5).
- **No Metadata Pointer Support**: Metadata cannot be transferred from a separate buffer.
- **SGL Requirement**: SGLs required for all commands (Admin, I/O, Fabrics); PRPs are not supported.
- **No Completion Queue Flow Control**: Host must ensure available CQ slots before submitting commands.
- **Optional Submission Queue Flow Control**: Can be disabled if host and controller agree; host must ensure available SQ slots.

---

## 2.2.1 Fabrics and Transports

- **Layering**: NVMe over Fabrics uses protocol layering (Figure 8). Core architecture is transport-independent; NVMe Transport binding specs define transport-specific details.
- **Scope Exclusion**: Fabric Protocol and Physical layers (e.g., Ethernet, InfiniBand) are outside NVMe spec scope.

> 🖼️ **Figure 8**: NVMe over Fabrics Layering (refer to image)

---

## 2.2.2 NVM Subsystem Ports for Fabrics

- **Controllers per Subsystem**: 1 to (64 Ki - 16) controllers.
- **Ports per Subsystem**: 1 to 64 Ki NVM subsystem ports.
- **Port Definition**: Protocol interface between NVM subsystem and fabric; composed of one or more physical interfaces (e.g., aggregated Ethernet links).
- **Port Identifier (Port ID)**: 16-bit identifier.
- **Identification**: NVM Subsystem identified by NQN + Port ID.
- **Transport Support**: A port may support multiple NVMe Transports (e.g., iWARP and RoCE) if binding specs exist.
- **Controller Binding**: Controller bound to one NVM subsystem port; may be assigned flexibly, but once connected, bound to single port.
- **Host Association**: One controller associated with exactly one host at a time.
- **Multi-Path Support**: Multiple hosts can connect to different controllers via same port; multi-path I/O and namespace sharing follow memory-based model.

---

## 2.2.3 Discovery Service

- **Purpose**: Enables host to discover NVM subsystems with accessible namespaces.
- **Capabilities**:
  - Discover list of accessible NVM subsystems.
  - Discover multiple paths to a subsystem.
  - Discover statically configured controllers.
  - Optional: Establish persistent connection to Discovery controller.
  - Optional: Receive Asynchronous Event Notifications from Discovery controller.
- **Discovery Controller**: Only type supported; no other controller types.
- **Initial Discovery**: Method for obtaining Discovery Service info is implementation-specific (e.g., config file, OS property).

---

## 2.2.4 Capsules and Data Transfer

- **Capsule Definition**: NVMe unit of information exchange; types:
  - **Command Capsule**: Contains SQE (Admin/I/O/Fabrics command) + optional SGLs/data.
  - **Response Capsule**: Contains CQE (response to prior command) + optional data.
- **Data**: Any data transferred at NVMe layer (e.g., logical block data, command structures).
- **Capsule vs. Transport Units**: Independent of transport units (e.g., packets, frames); may span multiple units.
- **Command Capsule**:
  - **Minimum Size**: 64B (NVMe Transport binding-specific).
  - **Maximum Size**: NVMe Transport binding-specific.
  - **Format**: Figure 9.
- **Response Capsule**:
  - **Minimum Size**: 16B (NVMe Transport binding-specific).
  - **Maximum Size**: NVMe Transport binding-specific.
  - **Format**: Figure 10.
- **SGL Requirement**: All commands (Fabrics, Admin, I/O) require SGLs.
- **Data Transfer**:
  - For message-only and message/memory transport models: All SGLs must be sent within the command.
  - Transport may optionally support transferring data within command/response capsules.
  - SGLs specify data placement or transport-specific data transfer mechanisms (e.g., RDMA).

> 🖼️ **Figure 9**: Command Capsule Format (refer to image)  
> 🖼️ **Figure 10**: Response Capsule Format (refer to image)

---

## 2.2.5 Authentication

- **Supported Methods**:
  - **Fabric Secure Channel** (Section 8.3.5.1).
  - **NVMe In-Band Authentication**.
- **Requirement**: NVM subsystem may require one, both, or neither.
- **Discovery Service**: Indicates if fabric secure channel is required for subsystem.
- **Connect Response**: Indicates if NVMe in-band authentication is required for the controller.
- **Command Acceptance Rules**:
  - If fabric secure channel required: Controller rejects all commands until secure channel established.
  - If NVMe in-band auth required: Controller rejects all commands (except auth commands) on the queue until auth completes.

> 🔍 **Reference**: Section 8.3.5 for authentication details.

# 2.3 NVM_Storage_Model

## 2.3.1 Storage_Entities

The NVM storage model defines a hierarchical structure of storage entities:

- **NVM Subsystems** (Section 1.5.68)
- **Domains** (Section 3.2.5)
- **Endurance Groups** (Section 3.2.3)
- **Reclaim Groups & Reclaim Units** (Section 3.2.4)
- **NVM Sets** (Section 3.2.2)
- **Namespaces** (Section 3.2.1)

### Hierarchical Relationships:
- Each **Domain** is contained in a single **NVM Subsystem**.
- Each **Endurance Group** is contained in a single **Domain** and may contain:
  - One or more **NVM Sets**, or
  - One or more **Reclaim Groups**.
- Each **NVM Set** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.
- Each **Namespace** is contained in a single **NVM Set**.
- Each **Media Unit** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.
- Each **Reclaim Group** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.
- Each **Reclaim Unit** is contained in a **Reclaim Group**.
- A **Namespace** may span one or more **Reclaim Units** within **Reclaim Groups** in an **Endurance Group**.

**Media Units** and **Reclaim Unit Handles** are not shown in examples for clarity.

### Example Configurations:
- **Figure 11 (Simple)**: 1 Domain → 1 Endurance Group → 1 NVM Set → 1 Namespace.
- **Figure 12 (Simple)**: 1 Domain → 1 Endurance Group → 1 Reclaim Group → 1 Namespace (data placed per host write command).
- **Figure 13 (Simple)**: 1 Domain → 1 Endurance Group → 4 Reclaim Groups → 1 Namespace (data written to each Reclaim Group per host write).
- **Figure 15 (Complex)**: Multiple Domains → Multiple Endurance Groups per Domain → Multiple Reclaim Groups per Endurance Group → Multiple Namespaces per Endurance Group.

### Entity Naming Convention (Abc):
- **A**: Domain (capital letter)
- **b**: Endurance Group (digit)
- **c**: NVM Set (lower-case letter) OR Reclaim Group (digit or lower-case letter, max. per design)

### Configuration Notes:
- Support for **Endurance Groups**, **Reclaim Groups**, and **NVM Sets** is **optional**.
- Vendors may ship pre-configured NVM subsystems; customers may reconfigure.
- Typical configuration changes: **creation/deletion of namespaces**.
- NVM subsystems not supporting multiple NVM Sets or Endurance Groups **do not need to report** those entities.

---

## 2.3.2 I_O_Command_Sets

- Each **namespace** is associated with **exactly one I/O command set**.
- The association is **fixed at namespace creation** and cannot be changed.
- Examples:
  - **NVM Command Set**: accesses data as logical blocks.
  - **Key Value Command Set**: accesses data as key-value pairs.
- A controller may support **one or more I/O command sets**.
- Only namespaces associated with **enabled command sets** can be attached to the controller.
- Host commands to a namespace are interpreted based on its associated **I/O command set**.

---

## 2.3.3 NVM_Subsystem_Examples

### Simple Example (Figure 16):
- Single port, single domain.
- Domain contains 1 controller and storage media.
- All media in 1 Endurance Group → 1 NVM Set → 1 Namespace.

### Two-Namespace Example (Figure 17):
- NVM subsystem with two namespaces.

### Complex Example (Figure 18):
- Multiple domains, controllers, ports, and namespaces.

---

- **Figure 13**: Simple NVM subsystem (1 Domain → 1 Endurance Group → 4 Reclaim Groups → 1 Namespace).

# 2.4 Extended_Capabilities_Theory

## 2.4.1 Multi-Path I/O and Namespace Sharing

### Key Definitions and Requirements:
- **Multi-Path I/O**: Two or more independent paths between a host and a namespace.
- **Namespace Sharing**: Multiple hosts accessing a shared namespace via different NVMe controllers.
- Both require **two or more controllers** in the NVM subsystem.

### Architectural Details:
- **Single Function Device (Figure 19)**:
  - One controller, one PCI Express port, PCI Function 0.
  - Supports multiple private namespaces (e.g., NS A, NS B) with unique NSIDs (NSID 1, NSID 2).
  - **No multi-path I/O or namespace sharing** supported.

- **Multi-Function Device (Figure 20)**:
  - Two controllers on one PCI Express port, PCI Function 0 and 1.
  - Each controller has one private namespace and access to **shared namespace B**.
  - **Shared namespace uses same NSID across controllers** (NSID 2).
  - All controllers return identical `Identify Namespace` data for shared namespaces.
  - Shared namespace has a **globally unique identifier** (Section 4.7.1) to identify common access paths.

- **Dual-Port Subsystem (Figure 21)**:
  - Two independent PCI Express ports, each with a controller (PCI Function 0).
  - Each port has independent **PCI Express Fundamental Reset** and reference clock.
  - Reset on one port **does not affect** the other controller or shared namespace.
  - Supports multi-path I/O and I/O sharing; may connect to same or different Root Complexes.

- **SR-IOV Subsystem (Figure 22)**:
  - One Physical Function (PF) and four Virtual Functions (VFs), each with an NVMe controller.
  - Each controller has a private namespace and access to **shared namespace F**.
  - All controllers use same NSID for shared namespace.
  - Behavior consistent with other examples.

### Operational Rules:
- **NSID Usage**: Must be consistent across all controllers accessing the same shared namespace.
- **Identify Data**: Identical `Identify Namespace` data returned by all controllers accessing shared namespace.
- **Write Atomicity**: Operations are atomic at the **write atomicity level of the submitting controller** (Section 3.4.3). Atomicity levels **may differ** across controllers.
- **Command Ordering**: Host must enforce ordering requirements for commands across different controllers.

> **Note**: Examples are illustrative; not exhaustive. Configurations may include multiple ports with SR-IOV.

## 2.4.2 Asymmetric Controller Behavior

### Key Requirement:
- **Asymmetric behavior**: Namespace access characteristics (e.g., performance) may vary due to:
  - Internal NVM subsystem configuration, or
  - Controller used (e.g., Fabrics).

### Support:
- Systems supporting asymmetric behavior may implement **Asymmetric Namespace Access Reporting** (Section 8.1.1).

---

title: NVM_Express_Architecture

# 3 NVM_Express_Architecture

## 3 NVM Express Architecture

> **Section ID**: 3 | **Page**: 61-61

This section introduces the **NVM Express (NVMe)** architecture, a high-performance, scalable interface designed for non-volatile memory (NVM) devices such as SSDs. The architecture defines a standard for managing and accessing NVM resources using PCIe as the physical transport.

### Key Architectural Components

- **Host Controller Interface (HCI)**: The NVMe specification defines the interface between the host system and the NVM subsystem, enabling efficient command submission and completion.
- **Command Queueing**: NVMe supports multiple I/O queues (up to 65,535) for parallel command processing, enabling high throughput and low latency.
- **Queue Pair (QP) Structure**: Each I/O queue is paired with a completion queue (CQ), allowing asynchronous command processing.
- **Doorbell Registers**: Used to signal the controller when new commands are available or when completions are ready to be processed.

### Core Requirements

- **Minimum Queue Configuration**: A minimum of 1 I/O queue and 1 completion queue is required. The default number of queues is 1 I/O queue and 1 CQ.
- **Maximum Queue Configuration**: Supports up to **65,535 I/O queues** and **65,535 completion queues**.
- **Command Submission and Completion**: Commands are submitted via Submission Queues (SQs), and completions are reported via Completion Queues (CQs).
- **Queue Size**: Each queue can have up to **65,535 entries**.

### Data Structures

- **Command Format**: Commands are 64 bytes in size.
- **Completion Format**: Completion entries are 16 bytes in size.
- **Doorbell Registers**: 32-bit registers used to notify the controller of new commands or completions.

### Performance and Scalability

- **Parallelism**: The architecture enables parallelism through multiple queues and queue pairs, reducing CPU overhead and improving I/O throughput.
- **Low Latency**: Direct memory access (DMA) and optimized command processing reduce latency compared to traditional storage interfaces.

### Table: Queue Configuration Limits

| Queue Type           | Minimum | Maximum     | Default       |
|----------------------|---------|-------------|---------------|
| I/O Submission Queue | 1       | 65,535      | 1             |
| Completion Queue     | 1       | 65,535      | 1             |
| Queue Entries        | 1       | 65,535      | 1024          |

### Summary

NVMe leverages PCIe for high-speed access to NVM devices, supporting up to **65,535 I/O queues** and **65,535 completion queues**, each with up to **65,535 entries**. The architecture employs command and completion queues with doorbell registers for signaling, enabling high throughput, low latency, and scalability for modern storage systems.

title: NVM_Controller_Architecture
summary:
# 3.1 NVM_Controller_Architecture Summary

## **Controller Models**

- **Static Controller Model**:  
  - State (e.g., Controller ID, Feature settings) is preserved:
    - Across **Controller Level Reset** (memory-based and message-based controllers).
    - From **prior associations** (message-based controllers).
  - Host can request a specific **Controller ID** (CNTLID) via Fabrics Connect command.

- **Dynamic Controller Model**:  
  - Controllers allocated **on-demand** with **no state preservation**.
  - All controllers for a specific host start with **identical state** (Feature settings, attached namespaces) when accessed via the same NVM subsystem port.
  - State may differ across different ports.
  - Changes to one dynamic controller **do not affect others**.
  - Host requests dynamic allocation by specifying **Controller ID = FF FFh**.

> **All controllers in an NVM subsystem must support the same model.**

---

## **Controller Types**

Three types of controllers exist (as shown in **Figure 23**):

1. **I/O Controller**:  
   - Supports **I/O commands** for accessing user data.
   - May support **management commands**.
   - Can support **multiple I/O Command Sets** (reported in Identify I/O Command Set data structure).
   - May have **different namespace attachments** (e.g., shared or private namespaces).
   - Example: Figure 24 shows 3 I/O controllers:  
     - Controller 1: Private A, Shared B  
     - Controller 2: Private C, Shared B  
     - Controller 3: Initially no namespaces; later attaches Shared B.

2. **Administrative Controller**:  
   - Supports **management capabilities only** (no I/O commands).
   - **No I/O Queues**; **no namespaces attached**.
   - Must support mandatory Admin commands (see **Figure 28**).
   - May support I/O Command Sets for **Admin commands only**.
   - Can be used for:
     - NVMe-MI health polling (Send/Receive).
     - Namespace management (Attachment, Management).
     - Virtualization management.
     - NVM Subsystem Reset (NSSR) and Shutdown (NSSD) if supported.
   - Can exist in NVM subsystems with or without storage medium (e.g., **Figure 26**).

3. **Discovery Controller**:  
   - Used **only for NVMe over Fabrics** to access **Discovery log page**.
   - **Must support only dynamic controller model**.

---

## **Controller Architecture Details**

### **Memory-Based (PCIe) Controllers**  
- Support **only static controller model**.
- Host submits commands via **pre-allocated Submission Queues**.
- Controller alerted via **SQ Tail Doorbell** writes (PCIe-specific).
- **Command processing order** is arbitrary (no ordering restrictions, except fused operations).
- **Command priority** determined by Submission Queue priority.
- **Arbitration** based on fairness/priority (section 3.4.4).
- Completions delivered via **Completion Queues**; host notified via transport-specific methods (e.g., PCIe interrupts).
- **Host creates I/O Queues** via Create I/O Submission Queue and Create I/O Completion Queue commands.

### **Message-Based (Fabrics) Controllers**  
- Use **Fabrics Connect command** to establish association.
- Association established when host connects to Admin Queue.
- **Only one association per controller at a time**.
- Association ends if:
  - Controller shutdown (section 3.6.2),
  - Controller Level Reset,
  - Admin Queue transport connection lost,
  - I/O Queue connection lost and no individual I/O Queue deletion support.
- No explicit “Disconnect” command; **Disconnect command deletes I/O Queue only** (section 3.3.2.4).
- Reconnect requires same Host NQN, NVM Subsystem NQN, Controller ID, and either same Host ID or 0h (if supported).

---

## **Key Requirements and Values**

| Requirement | Value/Condition |
|-------------|------------------|
| Controller ID for dynamic allocation | `FF FFh` |
| Controller ID field in Connect command | CNTLID (Figure 580) |
| Mandatory Admin commands for Administrative Controller | Defined in **Figure 28** |
| Queue creation commands | `Create I/O Submission Queue`, `Create I/O Completion Queue` (section 5.3.2, 5.3.1) |
| Discovery Controller model | Only **dynamic** allowed |
| Memory-based controller model | Only **static** allowed |
| I/O Controller namespace attachment | Can be private or shared; may vary per controller |

---

## **Figures Reference**

- **Figure 23**: Controller Types (I/O, Administrative, Discovery)
- **Figure 24**: NVM subsystem with 3 I/O controllers and shared namespace B
- **Figure 25**: NVM subsystem with 1 Administrative and 2 I/O controllers
- **Figure 26**: Administrative controller in subsystem without storage medium (for NVMe-MI enclosure management)

---

title: NVM_Subsystem_Entities
summary:
# 3.2 NVM Subsystem Entities Summary

## 3.2.1 Namespaces

### 3.2.1.1 Namespace Overview  
A **namespace** is a formatted block of non-volatile memory accessible by a host. Each namespace is identified by a **Namespace ID (NSID)**.

---

### 3.2.1.2 Valid and Invalid NSIDs  
- **Valid NSIDs**: Range from 1 to the value reported in the **Number of Namespaces (NN)** field in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).  
- **Broadcast NSID**: `FFFFFFFFh` refers to all namespaces.  
- **Invalid NSIDs**: Any value not in the valid range and not `FFFFFFFFh`.  
- Valid NSIDs may be:
  - **Allocated** or **Unallocated** (Section 3.2.1.3), and
  - **Active** or **Inactive** for a specific controller (Section 3.2.1.4).

---

### 3.2.1.3 Allocated and Unallocated NSID Types  
- **Allocated NSID**: Refers to an existing namespace.  
- **Unallocated NSID**: Does not refer to any existing namespace.

---

### 3.2.1.4 Active and Inactive NSID Types  
- For a specific controller:  
  - **Active NSID**: Namespace is attached to the controller.  
  - **Inactive NSID**: Namespace is not attached to the controller.  
- **Unallocated NSIDs** are inactive for all controllers.  
- An allocated NSID may be active for some controllers and inactive for others.

---

### 3.2.1.5 NSID and Namespace Relationships  

| Valid NSID Type | Relationship to Namespace | Reference |
|------------------|----------------------------|-----------|
| Unallocated      | Does not refer to any existing namespace | 3.2.1.3 |
| Allocated        | Refers to a namespace that exists in the NVM subsystem | 3.2.1.3 |
| Inactive         | Does not refer to a namespace attached to the controller | 3.2.1.4 |
| Active           | Refers to a namespace attached to the controller | 3.2.1.4 |

> **Note**: Inactive → if allocated: not attached; if unallocated: no namespace exists.

- **Command Behavior**:  
  - Inactive NSID → Abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.  
  - Invalid NSID → Abort with **Invalid Namespace or Format**.

---

### 3.2.1.6 NSID and Namespace Usage  
- **NSID uniqueness**:  
  - Required if **Namespace Management**, **ANA Reporting**, **NVM Sets**, or **Sanitize Namespace** are supported.  
  - Otherwise:  
    - Shared namespaces → must be unique.  
    - Private namespaces → not required to be unique.  
- **Identify Command Usage**:  
  - **CNS=0h**: Query individual NSIDs; non-zero response → active NSID.  
  - **CNS=2h**: Retrieve up to 1,024 active NSIDs (repeat if >1,024).  
  - **CNS=10h**: Retrieve up to 1,024 allocated NSIDs (repeat if >1,024).  
- **NSID persistence**: May change across power-off; recommend static NSIDs.  
- **Namespace identification**: Use **UUID**, **NGUID**, or **EUI64** fields for consistency.  
- **UIDREUSE bit** in NSFEAT indicates NGUID/EUI64 reuse.  
- **ANA Reporting** supported if **ANARS bit = 1** in CMIC field (Figure 328).  
- **Namespace-I/O Queue relationship**: Host-defined; controller must support access to any attached namespace from any I/O Submission Queue.

---

### 3.2.1.7 I/O Command Set Associations  
- Each namespace is associated with **exactly one I/O Command Set**.  
- I/O Command Set determined by NSID in the command.  
- NVM subsystem may contain namespaces with different I/O Command Sets.  
- Controllers support attached namespaces using I/O Command Sets indicated in the **I/O Command Set Profile** (Section 5.2.26.1.17).

---

## 3.2.2 NVM Sets  

An **NVM Set** is a logical (and potentially physical) grouping of NVM. One or more namespaces can be created within an NVM Set, inheriting its attributes. A namespace must reside entirely within one NVM Set.

---

### NVM Set Attributes  
- **NVM Set Identifier**: 16-bit unique ID (0h reserved).  
- **Attributes reported via Identify (CNS=04h)**:  
  - NVM Set ID  
  - Optimal write size  
  - Total capacity  
  - Unallocated capacity  

---

### NVM Set Association  
- **Namespace → NVM Set**: Reported in **Identify Namespace** data structure.  
- **Create Namespace**: Host specifies target NVM Set ID.  
- **Host creates NVM Set**: Via **Create NVM Set** command → returns NVM Set ID.  

---

### NVM Set Awareness in Commands  
- Commands using NVM Set Identifier:  
  - **Identify** (Namespace & NVM Set List)  
  - **Capacity Management** (Create/Delete NVM Set)  
  - **Namespace Management** (Create action)  
  - **Get Features/Set Features** (Read Recovery Level, Predictable Latency Mode Config/Window)  
  - **Connect**  
  - **Create I/O Submission Queue**  
  - **Get Log Page** (Predictable Latency Per NVM Set)  

> See Table 3.2.2_NVM_Sets.

---

### Requirements if NVM Sets are Supported  
All controllers must:  
- Set **NVM Sets bit = 1** in Controller Attributes (CTRATT, Figure 328).  
- Support NVM Set ID in all applicable commands.  
- Support **NVM Set List** (CNS=04h).  
- Report NVM Set ID in Identify Namespace.  
- Support **Endurance Groups**.  
- Report **Endurance Group** for each NVM Set.

> If not supported → NVM Set ID must be 0h.

---

## 3.2.3 Endurance Groups  

Each **NVM Set** is associated with **exactly one Endurance Group** (16-bit ID, 0h reserved).

---

### Endurance Management  
- **Same Endurance Group ID**: Endurance managed across multiple NVM Sets.  
- **Unique Endurance Group ID**: Endurance managed locally within one NVM Set.  
- If NVM Sets not supported:  
  - Endurance Groups supported → managed within each group.  
  - No Endurance Groups → managed within the domain.  
- An Endurance Group belongs to **only one domain** (Section 3.2.5).

---

### Endurance Group Identifier Usage  
- Required fields: abort with **Invalid Field in Command** if 0h.  
- Information available via **Endurance Group Information log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.10).

> Example: NVM Set A & B → Endurance Group Y; NVM Set C → local group.

title: NVM_Queue_Models
summary:
# 3.3 NVM Queue Models

## Overview

NVM Express uses a paired Submission and Completion Queue mechanism. In the **memory-based transport model (PCIe)**, multiple Submission Queues may share a single Completion Queue. In the **message-based transport model (Fabrics)**, each Submission Queue maps to one Completion Queue.

---

## 3.3.1 Memory-based Transport Queue Model (PCIe)

### 3.3.1.1 Queue Setup and Initialization

Host must follow these steps to initialize queues:

1. Configure Admin Queue attributes (AQA, ASQ, ACQ).
2. Set I/O Submission (CC.IOSQES) and Completion (CC.IOCQES) Queue sizes.
3. Submit **Set Features** command with Number of Queues attribute to request I/O queues. Controller returns allocated number.
4. Check **CAP.MQES** (max entries per queue) and **CAP.CQR** (physically contiguous requirement).
5. Create I/O Completion Queues using **Create I/O Completion Queue** command.
6. Create I/O Submission Queues using **Create I/O Submission Queue** command.

> All queues must be created within controller’s allocation and queue attribute limits.

---

### 3.3.1.2 Queue Usage

- **Submitter** (host) uses **Tail pointer** to write entries. Increments Tail after each write; rolls to zero if exceeds queue size.
- **Consumer** (controller) uses **Head pointer** to read entries. Increments Head after consumption; rolls to zero if exceeds queue size.
- Host writes **Submission Queue Tail Doorbell** to signal new entries; writes **Completion Queue Head Doorbell** to signal consumed entries.

> Invalid doorbell writes trigger asynchronous event with status **Invalid Doorbell Write Value** → associated queue is deleted/recreated.

- Host checks **Phase Tag (P) bit** in Completion Queue entries to detect new completions.
- Controller uses **SQ Head Pointer (SQHD)** in CQE to notify host of consumed submission entries.
- A submission entry is **submitted** when doorbell is written to move Tail pointer to/past the entry slot.
- An entry is **consumed** when CQE indicates Head pointer has moved past its slot.

> **After submission but before consumption**, altering a submission entry → undefined behavior.  
> **After posting but before consumption**, altering a completion entry → undefined behavior.

### 3.3.1.2.1 Completion Queue Flow Control

If Completion Queue is full (no free slots), controller:
- Shall not post status to that queue.
- May stop processing new submission entries for that queue.
- Shall continue processing for other Submission Queues.

---

### 3.3.1.3 Queue Abort

To abort all commands in a Submission Queue, host can:

- Issue **Cancel command** with:
  - `Cancel Action = Multiple Command Cancel`
  - `NSID = FFFFFFFFh`
- OR issue **Delete I/O Submission Queue** → wait for success → recreate with **Create I/O Submission Queue**.

> If host loses communication before receiving completions or delete success, must follow steps in **section 9.6** to avoid data corruption.

---

### 3.3.1.4 Empty Queue

Queue is **Empty** when **Head = Tail**.  
> See Figure 73.

---

### 3.3.1.5 Full Queue

Queue is **Full** when **Head = Tail + 1** (modulo queue size).  
Number of entries when full = queue size - 1.  
> See Figure 74.

---

## 3.3.2 Message-based Transport Queue Model (Fabrics)

Queues are unidirectional communication channels for sending **capsules** between host and controller:

- Host → Controller: **Command capsules** via Submission Queues.
- Controller → Host: **Response capsules** via Completion Queues.

Queues created in pairs using **Connect command**.

### 3.3.2.1 Capsules and Data Transfers

A **capsule** is an NVMe unit of data (commands, responses, SGLs, data).

- Admin queue capsule size is **fixed** (defined in Transport binding spec).
- I/O command capsule size is **indicated by controller** in Identify Controller data.
- Controller supports **SGL-based data transfers** for Admin and I/O queues.
- Data may be transferred **within capsule** or via **memory transactions**, per SGL descriptors.
- Unused capsule fields → undefined value; must not be interpreted.

### 3.3.2.1.1 Command Capsules

- Sent from host to controller.
- Contains 64-byte **Submission Queue Entry (SQE)**.
- May include data or SGLs.
- **Command Identifier** must be unique per queue for outstanding commands.
- SGL descriptor in SQE contains **Offset** for data blocks.

> See Figure 75.

### 3.3.2.1.2 Response Capsules

- Sent from controller to host.
- Contains **Completion Queue Entry (CQE)**.
- May include data.
- CQE corresponds to previously submitted command capsule.

> (Note: Description truncated in source; full details in specification.)

# 3.4 Command Processing Summary

## 3.4.1 Command Ordering Requirements
- Commands not part of a fused operation and complying with atomic operation requirements are processed independently.
- No ordering guarantees between commands targeting the same LBA (e.g., Read and Write to LBA x).
- Host/application must enforce ordering if required.

## 3.4.2 Fused Operations
- Optional feature indicated in **FUSES field** (Identify Controller, Figure 328).
- Controlled via **FUSE field** in Command Dword 0 (Figure 91):
  - `00b`: Normal operation.
  - `01b`: First command in fused operation.
  - `10b`: Second command in fused operation.
- Requirements:
  - Commands executed as atomic unit (in sequence, no interleaving).
  - Error in first command → abort second.
  - Error in second command → completion status of first is defined per command set.
  - Commands must be adjacent in Submission Queue (wrapping allowed).
  - Memory-based: Same doorbell update for both.
  - Message-based: Commands submitted in-order.
  - Abort requires separate Abort command for each.
  - One Completion Queue entry per command.

## 3.4.3 Atomic Operations
- Definition is **command set specific**.
- Refer to respective NVM Express I/O Command Set specification for details.

## 3.4.4 Command Arbitration
- Controller selects commands from submitted pool using vendor-specific algorithm.
- Command processing begins when controller accesses/modifies state (features, user data).
- Command completed when Completion Queue entry is posted.
- **Candidate command**: Submitted and ready for processing.
- **Arbitration** selects Submission Queue for next processing.
- **Arbitration Burst**: Max commands processed from same queue before re-arbitration.

### 3.4.4.1 Round Robin Arbitration
- All Submission Queues (including Admin) treated with equal priority.
- Round-robin among queues; multiple commands per queue per round based on Arbitration Burst.

### 3.4.4.2 Weighted Round Robin with Urgent Priority Class
- Three strict priority classes:
  1. **Admin** (highest) — Admin Submission Queue.
  2. **Urgent** — I/O queues with urgent priority (processed after Admin, before weighted levels).
  3. **Weighted Round Robin** — High/Medium/Low levels, managed by host via Set Features.
- Within weighted levels: Round-robin among queues of same level.
- Max commands per queue per round = `min(Arbitration Burst, remaining credits)`.

### 3.4.4.3 Vendor Specific Arbitration
- Optional; outside scope of specification.

## 3.4.5 Outstanding Commands
A command is **outstanding** if:
- Submitted by host.
- Not yet completed.
- Not marked as non-outstanding by any of the following host actions:
  - Receives completion.
  - Receives successful Abort completion with **Immediate Abort Not Performed** bit = 0.
  - Receives successful Cancel completion with **Commands Aborted** = `1h` and Action Code = Single Command Cancel.
  - Reads CSTS.RDY = 0 (controller not ready) and command is not Fabrics.
  - Reads CSTS.SHST = `10b` (shutdown complete) and command is not Fabrics.
  - (Memory-based) Deletes I/O Submission Queue used by command.
  - (Message-based) Disconnects queue or restores communication after loss.

> **Note**: Once a command ceases to be outstanding, further processing by controller is impossible.

# 3.5 Controller Initialization

## 3.5.1 Memory-based Controller Initialization (PCIe)

### Key Steps:
1. Wait for `CSTS.RDY` to become `0` (reset complete).
2. Configure Admin Queue: Set `AQA`, `ASQ`, `ACQ`.
3. Initialize `CC.CSS` based on `CAP.CSS`:
   - `CAP.CSS.NOIOCSS=1` → `CC.CSS = 111b`
   - `CAP.CSS.IOCSS=1` → `CC.CSS = 110b`
   - `CAP.CSS.IOCSS=0` and `CAP.CSS.NCSS=1` → `CC.CSS = 000b`
4. Configure `CC.AMS` (arbitration) and `CC.MPS` (memory page size).
5. Enable controller: Set `CC.EN = 1`.
6. Wait for `CSTS.RDY = 1` (controller ready).
7. Issue Identify command (CNS 01h) for controller config.
8. For IOCSS:
   - Issue Identify (CNS 1Ch) and Set Features (FID 19h) to select I/O Command Set profile.
9. For each enabled I/O Command Set:
   - Issue Identify (CNS 07h) for Active NSID list.
   - For each NSID:
     - If NVM-based: Issue Identify (CNS 00h).
     - Issue Identify for I/O Command Set-specific and independent data structures (refer to Figure 326).
10. Determine supported I/O queues via Set Features (Number of Queues). Configure interrupt registers (MSI/MSI-X).
11. Allocate I/O Completion Queues using Create I/O Completion Queue.
12. Allocate I/O Submission Queues using Create I/O Submission Queue.
13. Enable asynchronous events via Set Features and Asynchronous Event Request commands (after `CSTS.RDY=1`).

**Note**: Same steps apply for exiting D3 power state.

---

## 3.5.2 Message-based Controller Initialization (Fabrics)

### Key Steps:
1. Establish NVMe Transport connection with NVM subsystem.
2. Create Admin Queue via Fabrics Connect command.
3. Perform NVMe authentication if required (Section 8.3.5.2).
4. Determine controller capabilities (Property Get).
5. Initialize `CC.CSS` as in PCIe (see above).
6. Configure `CC.AMS` and `CC.MPS`.
7. Enable controller: Set `CC.EN = 1`.
8. Wait for `CSTS.RDY = 1`.
9. Issue Identify (CNS 01h) for controller config.
10. For IOCSS:
    - Issue Identify (CNS 1Ch) and Set Features (FID 19h).
11. For each enabled I/O Command Set:
    - Issue Identify (CNS 07h).
    - For each NSID:
      - Issue Identify (CNS 00h) if NVM-based.
      - Issue Identify for I/O-specific and independent data structures (Figure 326).
12. Determine:
    - Max I/O queue size: `CAP.MQES`.
    - Number of I/O queues: Set Features (Number of Queues).
13. Create I/O Submission/Completion Queue pairs via Connect command (Section 6.3).
14. Enable asynchronous events via Set Features and Asynchronous Event Request commands (after `CSTS.RDY=1`).

**Note**: Association must be removed if CC.EN not set within 2 minutes after association.

---

## 3.5.2.1 Discovery Controller Initialization

### Key Steps:
1. After successful Connect command:
   - Perform NVMe authentication if required.
   - Read Controller Capabilities property.
   - Write Controller Configuration property, including `CC.EN = 1`.
   - Wait for `CSTS.RDY = 1`.
   - Issue Identify commands for all applicable controller data structures.
2. Read Discovery log page (Section 5.2.12.3.3).

---

## 3.5.3 Controller Ready Modes During Initialization

### Two Modes:
- **Controller Ready With Media**:
  - All namespaces and media ready by `CSTS.RDY=1`.
  - No `Namespace Not Ready` or `Admin Command Media Not Ready` errors allowed for Admin commands.

- **Controller Ready Independent of Media**:
  - Namespaces/media may not be ready at `CSTS.RDY=1`.
  - Allowed to abort Admin/I/O commands with `Namespace Not Ready` or `Admin Command Media Not Ready` until `CRTO.CRWMT` time after `CC.EN=1`.

### Controller Ready Modes Supported (CAP.CRMS):
- **CAP.CRMS.CRWMS**: Controller Ready With Media Support (bit 0)
- **CAP.CRMS.CRIMS**: Controller Ready Independent of Media Support (bit 1)

**Rules**:
- `CAP.CRMS = 00b`: Not supported (older specs). CC.CRIME is read-only `0`.
- `CAP.CRMS = 01b`: Only Ready With Media mode. CC.CRIME is `0`.
- `CAP.CRMS = 11b`: Both modes supported. Host can select via `CC.CRIME` before enabling controller.

### Requirements for Command Processing:
- Non-Figure 84 Admin commands: must be processed error-free at `CSTS.RDY=1`.
- Figure 84 Admin commands: must be processed error-free within `CRTO.CRWMT` after `CC.EN=1`.
- All I/O commands: must be processed error-free within `CRTO.CRWMT` after `CC.EN=1`.

### Table: Admin Commands Permitted to Abort with Admin Command Media Not Ready

| Admin Command         | Additional Restrictions |
|-----------------------|-------------------------|
| Capacity Management   |                         |
| Device Self-test      | If testing namespaces, return error. |

*(Refer to Figure 84 for full list)*

title: Shutdown_Processing
summary:
# 3.6 Shutdown_Processing

## Overview

This section defines shutdown processing mechanisms for NVMe controllers and NVM subsystems. Two mechanisms exist: **Controller Shutdown** (Sections 3.6.1–3.6.2) and **NVM Subsystem Shutdown** (Section 3.6.3). Only one shutdown may be active per controller at a time. If an NVM Subsystem Shutdown is requested during a controller shutdown, it **overrides** the controller shutdown.

Shutdown progress is tracked via the **CSTS.SHST** field (Figure 42), and the **CSTS.ST** bit indicates the type of shutdown in progress. A host initiates:

- **Controller Shutdown** by setting **CC.SHN** (Figure 41).
- **NVM Subsystem Shutdown** by modifying the **NSSD property** or issuing an **NVMe-MI Shutdown command**.

**NVM Subsystem Shutdown is not supported** on NVM subsystems with only one controller (excluding virtual controllers) — refer to Section 8.2.6.

Figure 85 outlines state transitions based on **CC.EN**, **CSTS.RDY**, and **CSTS.SHST**.

---

## 📊 Table 3.6: Shutdown Processing States

| CC.EN | CSTS.RDY | CSTS.SHST | Controller able to process Admin and I/O commands⁴ | Media state | Controller ready to be powered off |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | 0 | 00b | no | any | implementation specific¹ |
| 0 | 0 | 01b | no³ | shutdown in progress | no |
| 0 | 0 | 10b | no | shutdown | yes |
| 1 | 1 | 00b | yes | initialization in progress or usable² | no |
| 1 | 1 | 01b | no³ | shutdown in progress | no |
| 1 | 1 | 10b | no | shutdown | yes |

### Notes:
1. After reset or power-on, controller may reinitialize media and cease being ready to be powered off.
2. If **CC.CRIME = 0**, media is usable; if **CC.CRIME = 1**, media is either initializing or usable.
3. During shutdown processing, commands may be aborted with **Commands Aborted due to Power Loss Notification**.
4. I/O commands are only processed by controllers supporting them; fabrics commands are always processed if supported.

---

## 3.6.1 Memory-based Controller Shutdown (PCIe)

### Normal Shutdown (CC.SHN = 01b)
1. Stop submitting I/O commands and allow pending ones to complete.
2. Delete all I/O Submission Queues (if present) — aborts remaining commands.
3. Delete all I/O Completion Queues (if present).
4. Set **CC.SHN = 01b**.
5. Controller signals completion via **CSTS.SHST = 10b** and **CSTS.ST = 0**.

### Abrupt Shutdown (CC.SHN = 10b)
1. Stop submitting new I/O commands.
2. Set **CC.SHN = 10b**.
3. Controller signals completion via **CSTS.SHST = 10b** and **CSTS.ST = 0**.

### Power-Off Readiness
Controller is ready to be powered off when **CSTS.SHST = 10b** and **CSTS.ST = 0**, regardless of **CC.EN**.

### Post-Shutdown Reinitialization
To resume operation:
- If **CC.EN = 1**: Perform **Controller Level Reset**, then reinitialize.
- If **CC.EN = 0**: Either:
  - Perform Controller Level Reset, then reinitialize; OR
  - Set **CC.EN = 1** and **CC.SHN = 00b** in a single write → controller clears **CSTS.SHST = 00b**.

### Power Scope (CAP.CPS)
- **00b (Not Reported)** or **01b (Controller scope)**: Wait until **CSTS.SHST = 10b**.
- **10b (Domain scope)**: Wait until **all controllers** in domain report **CSTS.SHST = 10b**.
- **11b (NVM subsystem scope)**: Wait until **all controllers** in NVM subsystem report **CSTS.SHST = 10b**.

### Timing
Host should wait at least **RTD3 Entry Latency** (from Identify Controller, Figure 328) — if 0h, wait **1 second**.

### Important
Do **not disable controller** (via CC.EN) during shutdown — may delay processing.

---

## 3.6.2 Message-based Controller Shutdown (Fabrics)

### Shutdown Initiation
Use **Property Set command** to set:
- **CC.SHN = 01b** (normal shutdown)
- **CC.SHN = 10b** (abrupt shutdown)

### Post-Shutdown Behavior
- Controller processes **only Fabrics commands** until reset or removed.
- Keep Alive timer is **disabled**.
- Host may either disconnect at transport level or poll **CSTS.SHST** for completion.

### Reinitialization
Same as 3.6.1 — requires Controller Level Reset or single write setting **CC.EN = 1** and **CC.SHN = 00b**.

### Note
**CC.EN is not used for shutdown** — it triggers Controller Reset.

---

## 3.6.3 NVM Subsystem Shutdown

### Overview
Initiates shutdown of **all controllers** in a domain or NVM subsystem from a single controller.

### Requirements
- Controller must set **CAP.NSSS = 1** to indicate support.
- NVM Subsystem Shutdown is **not supported** on subsystems with only one controller (excluding virtual controllers).

### Enhancement
New functionality differences from revision 2.0 are indicated via the **NVM Subsystem Shutdown Enhance...** bit (partial content truncated).

### Interaction
Interacts with Power Loss Signaling — see Section 8.2.5.

---

## Key Definitions & Requirements Summary

- **CSTS.SHST = 10b** → shutdown complete.
- **CSTS.ST = 0** → shutdown type cleared.
- **CC.SHN** = 01b (normal), 10b (abrupt).
- **CAP.CPS** determines power scope: 00b/01b (controller), 10b (domain), 11b (NVM subsystem).
- **RTD3 Entry Latency** ≥ 0h → wait 1 second.
- During shutdown: **abort commands** with “Commands Aborted due to Power Loss Notification”.
- **NVM Subsystem Shutdown overrides Controller Shutdown**.
- **Only one shutdown** per controller allowed.

```markdown
# 3.7 Resets

## 3.7.1 NVM Subsystem Reset

### 3.7.1.1 Single Domain NVM Subsystems
- **Scope**: Entire NVM subsystem when no multiple domains are supported.
- **Initiation Conditions**:
  - Main power applied.
  - Writing `4E564D65h` ("NVMe") to NSSR.NSSRC field.
  - Request via NVM Express Management Interface.
  - Vendor-specific event.
- **Actions on Reset**:
  - Controller Level Reset (CLR) on all controllers.
  - Disable Persistent Memory Region for all controllers.
  - Transport-specific actions per applicable NVMe Transport spec.
- **Reporting**: CSTS.NSSRO field indicates reset occurred during power-on.
- **Host Initiation**: Optional capability indicated by CAP.NSSRS; may be restricted for safety.
- **Vendor Event Purpose**: Recover from fatal hardware/firmware errors.

### 3.7.1.2 Multiple Domain NVM Subsystems
- **Scope**: Either individual domain or entire subsystem (depending on implementation).
- **Initiation Conditions** (for domain reset):
  - Power applied to domain.
  - Writing `4E564D65h` to NSSR.NSSRC of any controller in domain.
  - Vendor-specific event within domain.
- **Actions on Reset**: Same as single domain (CLR on all domain controllers, disable PMR, transport actions).
- **Reporting**: CSTS.NSSRO indicates reset during power-on.
- **Host Initiation**: Optional, indicated by CAP.NSSRS; may be restricted per domain.

## 3.7.2 Controller Level Reset (CLR)

### Initiation Methods:
- NVM Subsystem Reset.
- Controller Reset (host clears CC.EN to ‘0’).
- Cross-Controller Reset command (Section 5.4.3).
- Transport-specific resets (per applicable NVMe Transport spec).

### CLR Actions:
- Stop processing all outstanding Admin/I/O commands.
- Delete all I/O Submission and Completion Queues.
- Set CSTS.RDY bit to ‘0’.
- Reset all NVMe controller properties (except specified exceptions).

### Exceptions:
- **Memory-based controllers**:
  - **CLR via Controller Reset**: Admin Queue (AQA, ASQ, ACQ), PMR properties (PMRCAP, PMRCTL, PMRSTS, PMREBS, PMRSWTP, PMRMSCU, PMRMSCL), CMBMSC not reset.
  - **CLR via Function Level Reset**: Only CMBMSC not reset.
- **Message-based controllers**: No exceptions.

### Transport Properties:
- Reset per applicable NVMe Transport binding spec (e.g., PCIe registers).

### Post-CLR Behavior:
- If media not usable and NVM Subsystem Shutdown not in progress/completed (CSTS.ST=0, CSTS.SHST=00b), controller may initialize media.
- Host recovery steps:
  1. Update transport/controller state.
  2. Set CC.EN to ‘1’.
  3. Wait for CSTS.RDY to become ‘1’.
  4. Configure via Admin commands.
  5. Recreate I/O queues.
  6. Resume I/O operations.

### Communication Loss:
- All CLRs except Controller Reset cause immediate loss of communication; controller cannot post aborts or completion entries.

### Message-based Controller Specifics:
- If CC.EN=0 during shutdown (CSTS.ST=0, CSTS.SHST=01b or 10b), Admin Queue remains connected for **at least 2 minutes**.
- After 2 minutes, association may be removed if controller not re-enabled.
- Does not apply if CSTS.ST=1 (NVM Subsystem Shutdown active).
- After Controller Reset, continues processing Fabrics commands (e.g., Property Get/Set).

### Host Recovery Recommendation:
- If host loses communication before receiving:
  - Completions for all outstanding commands, **or**
  - CSTS.RDY=0,
  → Strongly recommended to follow Section 9.6 to avoid data corruption.

## 3.7.2.1 Controller Reset
- Defined as host writing to CC to clear CC.EN from ‘1’ to ‘0’.
- Initiates CLR **unless** NVM Subsystem Shutdown is in progress/complete and CAP.NSSES=0 (Section 3.6.3).
- Effect is a **subset** of other CLRs:
  - Certain properties not reset (see Section 3.7.2).
  - Virtualization values unchanged (Sections 5.2.13.3.1, 5.4.10).
  - Feature values unchanged (Section 5.2.26.1.7).

## 3.7.3 Queue Level Reset of I/O Queues

### Purpose:
- Reset/reconfigure I/O Submission and Completion Queues.

### Process:
- **Memory-based transport**:
  1. Delete queue via Admin Queue (Delete I/O Submission/Completion Queue).
  2. Wait for completion.
  3. Recreate queue (Create I/O Submission/Completion Queue) with optional new attributes.
  4. For I/O Completion Queue reset: Delete associated I/O Submission Queues first, then recreate after I/O Completion Queue is recreated.
  - Undefined behavior if I/O Submission Queue has no matching I/O Completion Queue.

- **Message-based transport**:
  1. Send Disconnect command to I/O Queue.
  2. Wait for completion.
  3. Recreate using Connect command with QID ≠ 00h.
  4. Modify queue attributes via Connect.
  - If Disconnect not supported → queue level reset not supported.

### Precautions:
- Ensure queue is idle before deletion.
- Queue deletion aborts pending commands; completion entries may or may not be posted.
```

summary:
# 3.8 NVM_Capacity_Model

## Overview

The NVM Capacity Model defines hierarchical capacity reporting for entities within an NVM subsystem: **NVM subsystem**, **Domain**, **Endurance Group**, **NVM Set**, **Namespace** (with formatted storage), and **Media Unit**.

Capacity allocation follows a hierarchy:
- **Domain** → **Endurance Group** → **NVM Set** → **Namespace**
- Each level may not fully utilize its capacity.

### Key Rules:
- If **NVM Sets** are supported, then **Endurance Groups** must also be supported.
- If **Endurance Groups** are **not supported**, all `ENDGID` fields are set to `0h`.
- If **NVM Sets** are **not supported**, all `NVMSETID` fields are set to `0h`.
- **Media Units** are allocated to exactly one Endurance Group (and, if NVM Sets are supported, to exactly one NVM Set).
- Media Units connect to **Channels**, and each Channel connects to one or more Media Units.

### Host Management:
- **Capacity Management** (section 8.1.4) allocates:
  - Domain → Endurance Group
  - Endurance Group → NVM Set
  - Media Units → Endurance Group/NVM Set
- **Namespace Management** (section 8.1.16) allocates capacity to namespaces.

---

## Media Unit Organization Examples

### 3.8.2.1 Simple NVM Subsystem
- Single domain with 4 Channels, each with 4 Media Units.
- All Media Units in **one Endurance Group** and **one NVM Set**.
- Goal: **Maximum bandwidth** via simultaneous access to all Media Units.
- **Capacity Configuration Descriptor**:
  - 1 Endurance Group Configuration Descriptor → 1 NVM Set ID + 4 Channel Configuration Descriptors → each with 4 Media Unit Configuration Descriptors.

### 3.8.2.2 Vertically-Organized NVM Subsystem
- Single domain with 4 Channels (each with 4 Media Units).
- Each Channel’s Media Units form a separate **Endurance Group**, which maps to a unique **NVM Set**.
- Goal: **Isolation** among NVM Sets (reduced bandwidth per NVM Set).
- **Capacity Configuration Descriptor**:
  - 4 Endurance Group Configuration Descriptors → each has 1 NVM Set ID + 1 Channel Configuration Descriptor → each with 4 Media Unit Configuration Descriptors.

### 3.8.2.3 Horizontally-Organized Dual NAND NVM Subsystem
- Single domain, 4 Channels, each with 4 Media Units (NAND capable of SLC or QLC).
- Two **Endurance Groups**:
  - **Group 1** (SLC mode): Capacity Adjustment Factor ≈ **400**, 1 Media Unit per Channel → 4 total.
  - **Group 2** (QLC mode): Capacity Adjustment Factor = **100**, 3 Media Units per Channel → 12 total.
- Goal: **Max bandwidth** to SLC NVM Set, larger capacity to QLC NVM Set.

---

## Capacity Reporting

Capacity is reported based on supported features:

### For NVM Subsystems:
- **No domains**: Capacity in `Identify Controller` (`TNVMCAP`, `UNVMCAP`, `MEGCAP`).
- **With domains**: Capacity per domain via **Domain Attributes Entry** (`Total Domain Capacity`, `Unallocated Domain Capacity`, `Max Endurance Group Domain Capacity`).

### For Endurance Groups:
- Reported via **Endurance Group Information log page** (`TEGCAP`, `UEGCAP`).

### For NVM Sets:
- Reported via **NVM Set List** → `Total NVM Set Capacity`, `Unallocated NVM Set Capacity`.

### Capacity Management Table

| Entity being created / deleted | NVM Sets supported | Endurance Groups supported | Domains supported | Capacity information used¹ |
|-------------------------------|--------------------|---------------------------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Endurance Group**           | n/a                | Yes                       | No               | NVM subsystem³              |
|                               |                    |                           | Yes              | Domain⁴                     |
| **NVM Set**                   | Yes                | Yes²                      | n/a              | Endurance Group⁵            |
|                               |                    |                           |                  | NVM subsystem³              |
| **Namespace** (formatted)     | No                 | No                        | No               | NVM subsystem³              |
|                               |                    |                           | Yes              | Domain⁴                     |
|                               |                    |                           |                  | Endurance Group⁵            |
|                               | Yes                | Yes²                      | n/a              | NVM Set⁶                    |

> **Notes**:
> ¹ Used by host for creation/deletion checks and updated by controller.
> ² NVM Sets require Endurance Groups.
> ³ From `Identify Controller` (TNVMCAP, UNVMCAP, MEGCAP).
> ⁴ From **Domain Attributes Entry** (Total/Unallocated/Max Endurance Group Domain Capacity).
> ⁵ From **Endurance Group Information log page** (TEGCAP, UEGCAP).
> ⁶ From **NVM Set Attributes Entry** (Total/Unallocated NVM Set Capacity).
> ⁷ Created/deleted via **Capacity Management** (section 5.2.3).
> ⁸ Created/deleted via **Namespace Management** (section 8.1.16).

title: Keep_Alive
summary:
# 3.9 Keep_Alive Summary

## **Overview**

The Keep Alive capability uses a **Keep Alive Timer** on the controller to detect communication failures (e.g., transport, host, or controller failure) between host and controller. It is enabled if the **KAS field** (Keep Alive Support) in the Identify Controller data structure is non-zero (refer to Figure 328).

**Keep Alive Timeout Time (KATT)** is the time value set in the **Keep Alive Timeout (KATO) field**. The NVMe Transport binding defines:
- Minimum and maximum KATT values (if any),
- Whether Keep Alive Timer is **required** and **must be enabled**.
> Transports that do not detect connection loss promptly **must** support and enable Keep Alive Timer.

---

## **3.9.1 Keep_Alive_Timer_Configuration**

- Host configures KATO via:
  - **Fabric Connect command** (Section 6.3), or
  - **Set Features command** (Feature ID 0Fh, Section 5.2.26.1.8).
  
- **Validation Rules**:
  - If transport requires Keep Alive Timer and host attempts to disable (KATO=0h), command is **aborted** with status **Keep Alive Timeout Invalid**.
  - If KATO exceeds transport’s max, command is **aborted** with same status.
  - If KATO < minimum (transport or implementation), controller sets it to **minimum**.
- Controller **rounds up** KATO to nearest granularity reported in **KAS** field (Figure 328).
- Host retrieves current KATO via **Get Features** command.

---

## **3.9.2 Keep_Alive_Timer_Activation**

Keep Alive Timer is **active** if:
- `CC.EN == 1`
- `CSTS.RDY == 1`
- `CC.SHN == 00b`
- `CSTS.SHST == 00b`
- `KATO != 0h` (i.e., Keep Alive Timer enabled)

If inactive, **no Keep Alive Timeout** occurs.  
Activating the timer initializes it to KATO value.  
Host must ensure Admin Submission Queue has space for Keep Alive commands while timer is active.

---

## **3.9.3 Command_Based_Keep_Alive**

### **3.9.3.1 On Controller**

Controller uses Command Based Keep Alive if **TBKAS bit = 0** (Figure 328).

**Behavior**:
- Start timer when active (Section 3.9.2).
- Restart timer on:
  - Successful Keep Alive command completion, or
  - Successful Set Features (KATO ≠ 0).
- Expire timer if KATT elapses since last start/restart.
- Upon expiration → **Keep Alive Timeout** → perform cleanup (Section 3.9.5).

---

### **3.9.3.2 On Host**

Host may use Command Based Keep Alive regardless of controller mode.

**Best Practice**:
- Send Keep Alive commands **every KATT/2** to account for delays (transport RTT, processing, granularity).
- After successful Set Features (KATO ≠ 0), adjust timing as controller restarts timer.

**Host Implementation Example**:
- Uses **Keep Alive Send Timer** per controller.
- Tracks **last expired timestamp**.
- Timer **starts/restarts** on:
  - Timer enable, or
  - Successful Keep Alive completion, or
  - Successful Set Features (Feature ID 0Fh, KATO ≠ 0).
- Timer set to: `KATT/2 - elapsed_since_last_expired`, or 0 if elapsed > KATT/2.
- Timer **expires** → send Keep Alive command.
- **Detect Timeout**: If no completion received for Keep Alive command within KATT after sending.

---

## **3.9.4 Traffic_Based_Keep_Alive**

### **3.9.4.1 On Controller**

Controller supports Traffic Based Keep Alive if **TBKAS bit = 1** (Figure 328).  
If TBKAS=0 → uses Command Based Keep Alive (Section 3.9.3).

**Behavior**:
- Start **Keep Alive Timeout Interval** when timer becomes active.
- Timeout occurs if:
  - Timer active,
  - KATT elapsed since start of interval, and
  - **No Admin or I/O command** fetched during interval.
- End interval and:
  - **Do not start new interval** if timeout occurs or timer becomes inactive.
  - **Start new interval** if:
    - Timer active,
    - Keep Alive command completes successfully, or
    - Set Features (KATO ≠ 0) completes, or
    - KATT elapsed without timeout (i.e., command was fetched).

> **Maximum detection delay**: Up to **2 × KATT** after last command fetch (see Figure 90).

---

### **3.9.4.2 On Host**

Host **can only use Traffic Based Keep Alive** if controller also uses it.  
Do not use if controller uses Command Based (as controller expects Keep Alive commands).

**Behavior**:
- Same as Command Based Keep Alive (Section 3.9.3.2), except:
  - No Keep Alive command needed if Admin/I/O command was submitted and completed since last check.
  - Check for sending Keep Alive every **KATT/4** (instead of KATT/2) to prevent timeout.
- After successful Set Features, adjust check timing as controller restarts timer.
- If timeout detected and outstanding commands exist → strongly recommended to follow Section 9.6 to prevent data corruption.

> **Host Implementation Example**: Similar to Command Based, but with KATT/4 checking rate.

---

## **3.9.5 Keep_Alive_Timeout_Cleanup**

Upon Keep Alive Timeout, controller performs cleanup actions (refer to Section 3.9.5 — not detailed in excerpt).

---

## **Key Numerical Values**

| Parameter | Value/Constraint |
|-----------|------------------|
| **KATT** | Value in KATO field (rounded to granularity in KAS) |
| **KATO min/max** | Defined by NVMe Transport binding specification |
| **Send interval (Command Based)** | Every **KATT/2** |
| **Check interval (Traffic Based)** | Every **KATT/4** |
| **Max detection delay (Traffic Based)** | Up to **2 × KATT** (Figure 90) |

---

## **Figures**

- **Figure 90**: Illustrates periodic checks for timeout detection in Traffic Based Keep Alive. Shows **Check 3** detects timeout, giving **up to 2 × KATT delay** after last command fetch.  
  ![Figure 90](../section_images/Figure_3_9_4_1_Traffic_Based_Keep_Alive_on_the_Controller.png)
